segments.text: Review expressions and variables, then ask how a program can choose different actions when a condition changes.
Use a simple if statement. Read the code line by line, predict which branch runs, and then check the output.
Contrast if, elif, and else with examples that change only one Boolean condition at a time.
Show an indentation error and a logical error. Ask students to locate the first wrong line before correcting the code.
Turn repeated code into a while loop, then into a for loop. Compare when each form is easier to reason about.
Give a short loop exercise, check the trace table, provide feedback, and ask students to try again with a new bound.
